bramfatura.Cattaram.desc:
After a telefaturic dislocation, Cattaram appears as an endless mass of dust and stone. Rare hollows are linked by corridors that stretch for miles upon miles. There is no up, no down, no cardinal direction, only an infinite lattice of caverns. This bramfatura ripened inside the protoplanetary cloud and absorbed its "hard chemistry". Its metastuctures echo the crystalline lattices of the physical world. The shimmer of meta-gems gives Cattaram a deceiving beauty—the beauty of dead light steeped in the malice of the spirit world.

The barons of Cattaram—the Tanaraks—rule networks of tunnels branching from their throne-caves like veins and capillaries. Clusters of gemstones and veins of noble metametals hang from the walls and vaults. In these clusters, spirits heal after being destroyed in the physical realm. Young Kataphrons and Hypnexes look like heaps of uncut rock, but with time they "make" themselves—grinding edges, inlaying surfaces, guaging their proportions.

In the deepest part of the bramfatura, where even the memory of open space is gone, lies a circular hall. At its center floats the silicon throne of Morax, King of Cattaram. From the hall's single entrance stretches a long procession of Tanaraks, each come to offer the gavvakh they have gathered.

The coming of humankind to the Main Belt blinded Morax's court with a surge of new power. During the suppression of the miners' uprisings on the asteroids, blood mixed with suffering and seeped through the rock into the bramfatura. For the first time, Cattaram tasted true might. As the colonies grew, the spirits studied humankind, then learned to nudge them toward mutual slaughter and to push emotion to the brink of eccolapse. It was in the Belt colonies that scientists began to see what was happening not merely as "spatial fatigue syndrome", but as quasimorphosis.

To one who passes through telefaturic dislocation, this world seems silent at first. But the silence here is not peace—it is the patience of pressure. Cattaram does not hurry, it crushes with time. Everything here strives toward a single virtue: unbreakable form. And if one listens long enough, the stone itself begins to whisper its only word: "Harder".
bramfatura.Cattaram.name: Cattaram
bramfatura.Cattaram.shortdesc:
Lord: King Morax.

The source of metamatter,
the substance from which
quasimorphic reality is made.
bramfatura.Duggur.desc:
The telefaturic dislocation reveals the bramfatura of the Moon as an ocean of mist. Clusters of fortresses, monasteries, and prisons drift upon it, bound together by chains into heavy bunches. The metamatters that form Duggur look worn and ancient. Stone is wet and black, iron is rusted, and the light is blue and cold, like baptismal water before dawn.

The lunar bramfatura is a realm of temptation and punishment. Here, the Nobilises rule over small congregations of spirits known as Courts. Sweetness and pain are weighed on the same scales. Equites and Triarii receive pleasure and agony as equal rewards, while only the Servuses are granted pain alone.

Over Duggur reigns the Great Harlot Fokerma. Her Court is a narrow prison at the heart of a desolate cluster of twisted architecture. There, black pearls of lust and the silver of repentance are traded for gavvakh. The Equites and Nobilises bring their offerings of gavvakh to Fokerma as gifts, and in return she gives them passion and suffering—the double blessing of their eternal mistress. Fokerma rarely leaves her cell, yet the Moon's nearness to Earth lets her feel every surge of human anguish. Long ago, she was the first among the bramfaturas to sense the planet's potential. Twenty years after a vast outpouring of gavvakh that awakened her terrible hunger, she saw something rise beyond the border of the Silver Sphere—a spacecraft carrying a source of gavvakh within it. It soon vanished into Earth's atmosphere. But Fokerma knows how to wait.

The history of Duggur is not only a litany of waiting, but of victory as well. When the spirits of the Solar System realized that Gagtungr would not return, Urparp, Lugal of Ur, declared himself Emperor of the Solar System. Tezctlan and Fokerma joined forces and overthrew him—for a time. After that, Tezctlan descended to Earth, taking upon himself the fate of a hylonaut.

To one who comes from outside, Duggur feels like pressure on the chest and the taste of iron on the tongue. It smells of incense, half-rotted flesh, and blood on cold metal. This is a world where sin and repentance walk harnessed together, and temptation follows every prayer. Its nearness to Earth is no accident, but design. To decipher it would be to glimpse where Gagtungr lies—and what he truly is.
bramfatura.Duggur.name: Duggur
bramfatura.Duggur.shortdesc:
Lady: the Great Harlot Fokerma.

A bramfatura steeped in earthly
passion and suffering—Gagtungr's
outpost near Earth.
bramfatura.Flauros.desc:
After telefaturic dislocation, Flauros, the bramfatura of Jupiter, appears as a nocturnal forest. Heavy clouds hang low above it. Flauros lives by the rhythm of Jupiter's tempests: every storm marks the gathering of a clan bound to it, under the lead of its Ard Ri. The spirits renew their oaths, and the Curidhs, taking up their Gilles, set out to hunt.

Flauros remembers and honors the Empire of the Sun, yet its heart belongs to the night. The bramfaturas farthest from the Red and Gold Throne keep faith with Gagtungr almost by default. Here there are no passions like those that burn on the inner worlds. The vows once spoken by the Thanes of Flauros still echo in the thunder-layers of the bramfatura, and that thunder has never ceased. King Paimon, the horned god of Flauros, hides within the bone-white groves, ensuring that the ancient oaths are kept. He does not rule Flauros alone, but when any clan hears his step, the quarrels end, and all fall silent to hear the will of their lord.

When the Empire of the Sun fell and the thunder-roads fell silent for a moment, the forest did not vanish—it sank deeper into the night, gathering the clans anew while the other worlds quarreled over thrones. Since then, Flauros has served the Red and Gold Throne in its own way. By patiently awaiting the return of the true sovereign.

Even Earth knows Jupiter's soul. Echoes of Flauros grew into the physical world as the traditions of standing stones and nocturnal hunts. Classified AnCom corporation reports on political theology claim that anarcho-primitivism itself was inspired by Flauros. It remains an open question whether anarcho-capitalism was inspired by some other bramfatura.

The visitor feels Flauros in their chest—the echo of distant hunting horns resounding in the ribs. Jupiter is vast, and Flauros teaches vastness with it. If you endure long enough before its might, the night itself will grant you strength.
bramfatura.Flauros.name: Flauros
bramfatura.Flauros.shortdesc:
Lord: King Paimon.

A bramfatura whose radiance gave
rise on Earth to the dark and
dense forests.
bramfatura.Gannix.desc:
The bramfatura of Venus, revealed through telefaturic dislocation, unfolds as an endless maze of temple structures. From some unknowable "outside", vines, roots, and clouds of damp mist force their way in. Shades of green are everywhere. Even where green is not seen, it glimmers and breathes at the edge of awareness, warm resin and chlorophyll thick in the air.

Gannix is a realm of the free. Nothing matters more to the taltnoms than personal freedom. To feed their lords with power, they offer themselves in sacrifice again and again—assembling from the faintest remnants of being, only to live one more aeon in freedom before drawing the fatal lot once more.

The ruler of Gannix, Tezctlan, has returned from the physical world. He was a hylonaut—a quasimorph who dared to walk the Earth. One of only two lords of the bramfaturas ever to attempt it. It was a one-way journey. No one foresaw that the inhabitants of Earth would one day break free from their gravity well, and bring back those who had vanished within it.

Now, returned, Tezctlan builds the Emerald Empire. His fascination with humankind is open and undisguised. To him, they are an energy source, an instrument of worship, a reservoir for the grand work that waits to be done in the material world. Where other bramfaturas wait patiently for the seepage of gavvakh, Tezctlan creates the conditions for it himself.

He has taught the taltnoms to anchor themselves to the physical realm, through obelisks anointed with blood and tree sap. Through such nodes they can remain embodied for long spans and even act beyond the bounds of Venus itself.

Not all welcome this. The wild taltnoms, spirits of the groves, remember Gannix before the Empire—a feral world without a master, savage and utterly free. They whisper that their ruler has gone mad, that the tended garden is a prison built for the wild forest.

To humans, Gannix feels like pressure from something alive. Growth everywhere—the cycle of decay and sprouting. Gannix is life made into metaphor. The bramfatura smells of black soil and wet stone. Here, everything seeks to intertwine. It is a world where growth is a form of will, and will is a form of growth.
bramfatura.Gannix.name: Gannix
bramfatura.Gannix.shortdesc:
Lord: the Emerald Emperor, Tezctlan.

A bramfatura overflowing with life,
yet demanding unending sacrifice
to sustain its perpetual growth.
bramfatura.Olirna_Awakened.desc:
After the awakening of Olirna, telephaturic dislocation for the first time makes it possible to pass through what was once the impenetrable boundary of Saturn's bramfatura.

Olirna reveals itself as a realm of high, frozen plateaus, black crags, and richly adorned monastery-fortresses growing directly from mountain ledges. Above the passes hang weathered streamers like prayer flags, but the wind no longer carries any blessing from them. Between the mountain ranges lie empty valleys where the cold light of a distant star once gathered. Now even their floors are scored with furrows, as though something immense had drained the bramfatura's inner strength dry in a single draught.

Olirna was sealed away in the deep past, when the Solar System was only beginning to form its planets in the physical layer of reality. While other bramfaturas waged war, fractured, changed rulers, and sent hylonauts to Earth, it remained a closed vessel. Gavvakh was not stored here. Instead, in absolute stillness, another kind of power was gathered—cold, heavy, and capable of enduring for millions of years without loss. Through all those ages, the spirits of Olirna knew only service to an unseen force that had chosen them for a single purpose. Their world was harsh, but ordered. Now it is clear that all this ascetic discipline was merely preparation for the coming of something so utterly new that they could not grasp its meaning. Recently, the seal was broken, and in a single instant the strength accumulated over uncounted ages was drawn away, toward the Sun. Olirna was not destroyed, but hollowed out.

In the eyries of the mountain fortresses rule the dzongpons, lords without power. They have preserved the bearing of rulers, but they have long ceased to belong to themselves. Over the passes, shrieking from fortress to fortress, dart the dre, lesser winged spirits for whom enslavement changed nothing, because they have never known any other state. In the guard chambers, high towers, and lavishly adorned temple quarters stand the gangsengs, soft-footed servants of Olirna in whom the shadow of an older nobility can still be seen. Within the fortresses, before the dried reservoirs and in the halls of vows, among gilded shrines and painted murals, the damtsigs keep their vigil—spirits bound by oath, their promises seized by an alien will and turned toward another end. And leading the war-bands are the dapons, the knights of Olirna, who retain their training and ferocity but have been stripped of the inner core that once made them worthy of command.

Olirna is unlike the ordinary pandemoniums of the Inner System. What reigns here is not the exultation of savage cruelty stirred by the coming of humankind, but the numbed awareness of universal compulsion—of all things being driven toward the fulfillment of one and the same design along every line of fate. The cold that once formed the heart of the bramfatura has left its opened shell and gone to the distant star, there to lend Gagtungr visible force for what is yet to come.
bramfatura.Olirna_Awakened.name: Olirna
bramfatura.Olirna_Awakened.shortdesc:
A freezing bramfatura left with no
ruler, it served millions of years
as a sealed reservoir of power.
After its awakening and sudden
desiccation, its inhabitants remain
—slaves to an empty vessel.
bramfatura.Olirna_Sleeping.desc:
Telefaturic dislocation allows us to manifest only the boundary of Saturn's bramfatura: a condensed volume of extraordinary energy. But it is no vault of gavvakh. It is something else entirely. Every attempt to open a telefaturic passage into the bramfatura gutters out. The signal stratifies, and the dislocator's impeller spins idly.

Olirna does not answer. It is sealed against outside influence. The sensors the telefaturic equipment relies on to manage an in-bramfatura mission likewise return nothing of use—or rather, almost nothing. Analysis of the inbound stream suggests that something is at work within. The plots read like a slow transfer of mass, in no rhythm known to us.

The SBN network still holds records of the incident at Frantseva-7 Station. All signs point to a quasimorphic event. So Olirna is alive—or was. And there is a third possibility: that something completely different is happening inside.
bramfatura.Olirna_Sleeping.name: Olirna
bramfatura.Olirna_Sleeping.shortdesc:
A sleeping bramfatura. What occurs
within its bounds remains unknown.
bramfatura.Ron.desc:
After telefaturic dislocation, Ron appears as a mass of primal substrate—the raw foundation from which the bramfaturas of the Solar System were once woven. It is meta-metamatter—pure quasimorphic substance, the only true material in the universe. The physical world is merely its reverse side, the outer shadow of what unfolds within the bramfaturas. Over fourteen billion years, it has thickened and stagnated, warped by the shock of alien wars and cosmic collapse, turning into a mottled slurry—a quasimorphic mire where selfish, self-adoring spirits spawn of their own accord. Their feelings and motives are blurred, unknowable even to themselves.

The hylonauts of Ron are known to humankind by many names. In the Mediterranean, they are remembered as Titans—monsters that swallowed gavvakh by the cityful. They were subdued only by a new wave of hylonauts, arriving in the age of the Sun’s bramfatura decline.

The bramfatura is reluctantly "ruled" by the Grand Duke Bathin. In his formless stone castle upon an island in a black lake, he waits for his servants to bring him gavvakh. He took the throne after the king and his loyal followers withdrew into the Silver Sphere, and since then has shown no desire to rule. Spirits wander and battle freely across Ron's wastes, while the landscape itself grows darker with the bubbles where they are reborn again and again.

The arrival of humans on Vesta and Pallas shook Ron from its stupor. The spirits sensed in humankind an extraordinary density of gavvakh. Bathin ordered that this strength be brought to him. It stretches his shadow, gives him weight, and he dreams of greeting Gagtungr’s return as the rightful sovereign of the bramfatura. But with each passing age, his fear deepens—the fear that the true lords of Ron will come back.

If one listens closely, through the darkness of the lake, one can hear Bathin whispering the same words over and over: "Bring more." Ron lives on what sinks to the bottom, and on what humankind surrenders to its depths.
bramfatura.Ron.name: Ron
bramfatura.Ron.shortdesc:
Lord: the Grand Duke Bathin.

The sediment of the quasimorphic
world—all that was left over from
the ripening of the Solar bramfaturas
settles here.
bramfatura.Scrivnus.desc:
After telefaturic dislocation, Skrivnus reveals itself as a disfigured world stripped of any hint of hope. A colorless landscape stretches to the horizon. A lead-grey, perfectly still sea mirrors the tone of the sky. The dwellings of spirits are basins—enclosed hollows ringed by low yet impassable slopes.

In the age of the Solar Empire, Skrivnus was its prison. By Gagtungr's cruel decree, true lawbreakers were sent here. For billions of years, the spirits of this world did only one thing—they forged weapons from the metametals saturating the leaden soil. The curved scimitars of Shartmakhum, the dense cores of Gannix's clubs, the armor of Duggur—all were born in the pits of Skrivnus.

When humankind first appeared on Interamnia, Skrivnus felt joy for the first time—the joy of eccolapse. The early colonists and pirates were not meek. They gladly answered voices that called them toward violence. Gavvakh poured into Skrivnus like molten metal into a mold, and the wretched spirits felt a spark of life. At last, the weapons they had forged without purpose found a reason to exist. The second tide came with Geist. When Dilthey corporation activated the graviton generator there, a hollow bramfaturic shell formed around the artificial planet. Interamnia's closeness decided the rest—Skrivnus flooded the newborn sphere, and its joyless dominion expanded.

The metamatter here is steeped in secrets so deep that even the spirits who keep them—the Gremmugrats, the prison's primary inhabitants, who were once spirits of vastly different bramfaturas—can no longer remember what freedom means. The Tarkaors, prison-knights and personal executioners of Gagtungr, fight not to fulfill the essence of their bramfatura, but to guard the prison itself, as though the act of guarding were the purpose of being. The Karzurs, barons of Skrivnus, rule over clusters of cells. They collect gavvakh and feed it back into the bramfatura. No one knows who rules Skrivnus now. The barons only hope their offering is not in vain, that the gavvakh reaches its destination.

The private dungeon of Gagtungr holds one dreadful secret. Skrivnus smells of wet lead and cold ashen dust. Everything here bends under the weight of gravity. Speech sounds like the rolling of slag; a single step echoes for miles; memory itself settles like sediment. If one listens closely, there's an almost musical rhythm beneath these sounds, and it betrays the secret. The dim realization that Gagtungr never existed. The prison creates itself, without hope, without art. But no prison stands by itself. Even if Gagtungr does not exist, he will. And when he does, the weapons will finally be needed.
bramfatura.Scrivnus.name: Skrivnus
bramfatura.Scrivnus.shortdesc:
Lord: unknown.

The prison of the
quasimorphic world.
